chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Cate
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:**

Fifteen ways of spiritual progression are established within the intermediate state of the human mind. Four of these ways are uncorrupted and belong [GAP-1] to divine wisdom, ascending toward spiritual life itself. Eight further ways are [GAP-2] of mingled quality — partly of good, partly of evil — rising upward from that intermediate condition. Through these, whatever is of wisdom ascends and is set free; it is purified and passes in [GAP-3] to the doctrinal vessels that carry truth to the heavenly kingdom. But what is refuse — the residue of falsity and evil — is separated out and cast down into further states of bondage, and the remaining three ways of [GAP-4] spiritual refuse are expelled into the hells.

**¶3:**

[GAP-5] The three ways that belong to what is spiritually refuse, those that are drawn toward the hells, originate from what is merely corporeal and sensual in the will. The first of these is the lust for what violates divine order — the concupiscence that rules in human beings and in every sensual affection. The second is the [GAP-6] destruction that pervades all outward forms of life, which is the annihilation of good and truth — [GAP-7] by which every natural affection is consumed and laid waste. The third is the act of profanation, which [GAP-8] assaults the divine truth suffering within natural forms, and every external vessel of spiritual life — together with all remaining falsity and blasphemy that wounds the divine attributes themselves.

**¶4:**

These three ways lead into the hells. Every soul proceeds according to the quality of its life and its works — either toward spiritual life, or else toward spiritual death.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste are] discharged to the gehennas.

[The three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [destruction of] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [harms] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
Th[ese th]ree paths lead to the gehennas. Every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms these paths "belong to divine wisdom," and "to the" correctly links "belong" to "light" (= divine wisdom in the Kephalaia's natural register).
The spiritual reading says "of mingled quality — partly of good, partly of evil," and "mixed" is the standard Manichaean term for the state where light and darkness are commingled.
The spiritual reading says light "passes in to the doctrinal vessels," and "to the" correctly connects "go in" with "ships" (the Sun and Moon vessels that carry purified light).

The spiritual reading says "three ways of spiritual refuse are expelled into the hells," so in the natural register "waste are" completes "the other three paths of waste are discharged to the gehennas."
The spiritual reading confirms "The three ways that belong to what is spiritually refuse," and the paragraph opens by specifying these three paths of waste just enumerated.

The spiritual reading says "the destruction that pervades all outward forms of life, which is the annihilation of good and truth," and in the Kephalaia register "destruction of all bodies, which is slaughter" parallels the first path's noun-phrase structure.
The spiritual reading says "by which every natural affection is consumed," and "with which" is the standard Coptic-to-English rendering for the instrumental relative, matching "by which."

The spiritual reading says "assaults the divine truth suffering within natural forms," and "harms" is the appropriate Kephalaia-register verb for an action against the Cross of Light, distinct from "wounds" used later for blasphemy against the gods.
